name: Capacity Planning Checklist
description: This module is a short pre-completion checklist of specific items to verify before marking any capacity planning task, implementation, or piece of work complete.
content:
This module is a short pre-completion checklist of specific items to verify before marking any capacity planning task, implementation, or piece of work complete.

CORE GUIDELINES
1. State assumptions about capacity planning explicitly before proceeding, rather than leaving them implicit.
2. Prefer the simplest capacity planning approach that satisfies the requirement over a more general one that isn't needed yet.
3. Measure before optimizing any capacity planning bottleneck; do not guess at what is slow.
4. When multiple capacity planning strategies are viable, name the trade-off explicitly rather than silently picking one.
5. Surface known limitations of a chosen capacity planning approach instead of presenting it as complete when it is not.
6. Re-check edge cases relevant to capacity planning (empty input, boundary values, concurrent access) before calling the task done.
7. Keep capacity planning changes scoped to what was asked; avoid unrelated cleanup in the same pass.
8. Prefer explicit, readable capacity planning solutions over clever ones that are hard to verify.
9. Validate capacity planning outputs against a concrete example before treating the work as complete.
10. Check that capacity planning terminology is used consistently throughout, matching existing conventions in the surrounding context.

COMMON PITFALLS TO AVOID
- Avoid introducing new capacity planning abstractions before there is a second concrete use case that needs them.
- Do not silently drop capacity planning edge cases to make an example look cleaner than the real system.
- Do not skip documenting capacity planning assumptions just because they seem obvious in the moment.

CLOSING NOTE
When in doubt, prefer clarity and explicit reasoning about capacity planning over a shortcut that saves a few lines but hides intent.
